title: Derived-complete module complexes are closed under products and triangles
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be any ideal, and work in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived completeness means [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. (1) If $(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ is a countable family of derived $I$-complete objects, its product $\prod_{n\geq1}K_n$ [def-weil-category-product] is derived $I$-complete. (2) In any distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], if two of $X,Y,Z$ are derived $I$-complete, so is the third. These assertions require neither finite generation of $I$ nor boundedness of the complexes.

proof.text: Products of $A$-modules are exact: a product of injections is injective coordinatewise; a tuple in the kernel of a product map has a preimage coordinatewise in the corresponding images; and a tuple in a product of quotients has a tuple of lifts (choice). Thus the abelian category of $A$-modules has exact countable products. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] supplies countable products in $D(A)$, for arbitrary unbounded representatives. Clause (1) then supplies the multiplication-tower derived limits and says that any two choices are isomorphic. In particular the universal quantifier over such limits in [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex] is equivalent to vanishing of one choice.

proof.text: For each $f\in I$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-localization-tower-vanishing]. By [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], an object $L$ is derived $I$-complete exactly when every morphism $A_f[0][q]\to L$ is zero for every $f\in I$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$. The sign of the shift causes no restriction because $q$ ranges over all integers.

proof.text: Let $P=\prod_{n\geq1}K_n$, existing by step 1. Fix $f\in I$, $q\in\mathbf Z$ and $a:A_f[0][q]\to P$. Each composite $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ a$ is zero by completeness of $K_n$ and step 2. By the uniqueness clause of [def-weil-category-product], $a$ equals the zero morphism, which has the same composites with all projections. Step 2 now gives completeness of $P$. This argument uses no interchange of tensor products with infinite products.

proof.text: First, completeness is stable under every shift: the shift automorphism in [def-weil-triangulated-category] identifies maps $A_f[0][q]\to L[r]$ with maps $A_f[0]\lbrack q-r\rbrack\to L$, by applying $[-r]$. If $L$ is complete these maps vanish for all $f,q$, so step 2 makes $L[r]$ complete. For a distinguished triangle with complete first and third objects $X,Z$, fix $W=A_f[0][q]$ and $a:W\to Y$. Since $Z$ is complete, $v\circ a=0$. Clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $b:W\to X$ with $a=u\circ b$. Completeness of $X$ gives $b=0$, hence $a=0$. Step 2 proves completeness of $Y$. If instead $X,Y$ are complete, rotate once to $Y\to Z\to X[1]\to Y[1]$; its endpoints $Y,X[1]$ are complete, so the same middle-object argument proves completeness of $Z$. If $Y,Z$ are complete, rotate backwards to $Z[-1]\to X\to Y\to Z$ (up to the conventional signs); its endpoints $Z[-1],Y$ are complete, so the same argument proves completeness of $X$. These rotations are allowed by TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category].
